newsitem.title: UK: Pearson almost doubles half-year profits.
newsitem.headline: Pearson almost doubles half-year profits.

text.p: Pearson Plc, owner of the Financial Times newspaper and Penguin books, said Monday profit from continuing operations almost doubled to 65.5 million pounds ($107 million) in the first six months of 1997.
Pearson Chief Executive Marjorie Scardino, who called the better-than-expected figures a "first step," vowed to double the value of the company within five years.
"These results represent the first step in our commitment to improve the company's performance," said Scardino, who in January became the first woman to lead a top British company

She said in a statement that the goal was to double Pearson's value over the next five years and achieve annual double-digit earnings growth. The company has a market capitalisation of about 4 billion pounds ($6.5 billion).

Finance Director John Makinson said Pearson was actively reviewing a diverse portfolio of possible acquisitions that included a television production arm, the Madame Tussaud's wax museum and a 50 percent stake in London merchant bank Lazard Brothers.
He said decisions had already been made on the future of some businesses and added that the Pearson portfolio would have a different look within five years.
Pearson reported a surge in first-half profits at the Financial Times and a strong performance from Penguin as last December's acquisition of U.S. publisher Putnam Berkley was integrated swiftly.

Improper accounting at Penguin USA came to light earlier this year after going undetected since the early 1990s, but Pearson said it believed the 100 million pound ($163 million) provision taken in 1996 should cover the total losses.
